title: Authorisation and Licensing: The Regulatory Gateway
summary: A ten-module programme giving authorisation staff a structured, defensible methodology for assessing applications, key individuals, owners and changes at the regulatory gateway.
intro: This training programme equips authorisation staff to run the regulatory gateway well: assessing applications, business plans, owners and key individuals rigorously and consistently, so that only firms able to meet standards enter the market.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To equip authorisation and licensing staff with a structured, defensible methodology for assessing new applications and changes to existing firms. Participants leave able to scrutinise business plans and readiness, assess fitness and propriety, controllers and ownership, integrate financial crime checks and reach well-reasoned recommendations.
sections.What It Covers: The purpose and standards of the regulatory gateway, the application process, business plans and financial projections, organisational readiness, fit and proper assessment, controllers and change of control, beneficial ownership, financial crime checks, cross-border authorisation and passporting, and licence variations, conditions and decisions.
Intended Audience: Authorisation, licensing and registration staff assessing new applications and changes to existing firms
Fitness and propriety and governance specialists assessing controllers, directors and senior managers
Supervisors and financial crime specialists who contribute to authorisation decisions or take over newly authorised firms
Learning Objectives: Explain the role of the gateway in shaping the risk profile of the regulated population
Assess business plans, financial projections and organisational readiness
Apply consistent, defensible criteria to fitness and propriety and to proposed controllers
Trace beneficial ownership and integrate financial crime checks into the assessment
Evaluate cross-border applications and cooperate effectively with other authorities
Formulate and document authorisation recommendations, conditions and refusals
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Modules combine short input with sample applications, case studies and assessment exercises, ending in an end-to-end application workshop, and can be selected or tailored to the authority's own licensing regime.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of authorisation, supervision or financial crime work is helpful. No legal or accounting qualification is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision (2024)
IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
IAIS, Insurance Core Principles and Common Framework for the Supervision of Internationally Active Insurance Groups (ComFrame)
FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)

modules.title: The Regulatory Gateway: Purpose and Standards
modules.summary: Why authorisation is a critical gatekeeping function, the threshold conditions applicants must meet, and how authorities balance market access and innovation against risk.
objectives: Explain the purpose and standard of assessment at the gateway
Describe the threshold conditions and how they apply proportionately
Balance market access and competition against risk to customers and markets
syllabus: The gateway as the first and cheapest line of supervisory defence
Threshold conditions: legal status, resources, suitability and effective supervision
Proportionality across firm types, sizes and activities
International standards on licensing and authorisation

modules.title: The Application Process: From First Contact to Decision
modules.summary: How an authorisation process runs in practice, from pre-application engagement and completeness checks through information requests to the governance of the final decision.
objectives: Describe the stages of the application process and service standards
Manage pre-application engagement and information requests effectively
Identify common application weaknesses early
syllabus: Pre-application meetings and setting expectations
Completeness checks, statutory timelines and stopping the clock
Sources of evidence in an application and verifying them
Decision governance, escalation and recording reasons

modules.title: Assessing Business Plans and Financial Projections
modules.summary: A structured method for scrutinising an applicant's business plan, testing the credibility of financial projections and stress-testing growth assumptions.
objectives: Apply a structured framework to review a business plan
Assess the credibility of financial projections and capital adequacy
Stress-test growth and revenue assumptions
syllabus: Business plan review: market, model, customers and viability
Projections: revenue, costs, capital and liquidity
Red flags in projections and unsupported assumptions
Exercise: reviewing a sample business plan

modules.title: Organisational Readiness: Governance, Systems and Controls
modules.summary: How to judge whether an applicant will be ready to operate on day one, with adequate governance, staffing, systems, controls and real substance in the jurisdiction.
objectives: Evaluate governance arrangements and the allocation of responsibilities
Assess systems, controls, outsourcing and staffing readiness
Judge whether the applicant has genuine local substance
syllabus: Board composition, control functions and accountability
Systems, policies and procedures: designed or merely drafted
Outsourcing, group dependencies and substance requirements
Readiness gaps: conditions, phased authorisation or refusal

modules.title: Fit and Proper Assessment: Criteria and Evidence
modules.summary: The fitness and propriety framework for controllers, directors and senior managers, the evidence sources available, and how assessment differs at authorisation and on an ongoing basis.
objectives: Explain competence, capability and probity as distinct assessment strands
Identify and verify the evidence available on a candidate
Apply fit and proper assessment proportionately across roles
syllabus: Competence, capability, honesty, integrity and financial soundness
Evidence: CVs, references, disclosures and public record checks
Assessing fitness at authorisation and throughout tenure
Proportionality by role, firm size and risk

modules.title: Fit and Proper in Practice: Interviews and Difficult Cases
modules.summary: Using interviews to test competence and integrity, weighing adverse information fairly, and documenting consistent, defensible decisions in borderline cases.
objectives: Plan and conduct a fit and proper interview
Weigh adverse information consistently and fairly
Document a fit and proper decision that will withstand challenge
syllabus: Interview planning and questioning for competence and probity
Handling adverse information, non-disclosure and inconsistency
Consistency across candidates, roles and decision-makers
Case study: a borderline fit and proper assessment

modules.title: Controllers, Ownership and Change of Control
modules.summary: How to assess proposed controllers at authorisation and on a change of control, trace beneficial ownership through complex structures, and keep unsuitable owners out of the sector.
objectives: Explain what triggers a change-of-control assessment and the criteria applied
Trace beneficial ownership through layered or opaque structures
Formulate an outcome on a proposed change of control
syllabus: Notifiable changes of control, timelines and procedure
Assessing a proposed controller: reputation, financial soundness, plans
Trusts, nominees and layered structures as risk indicators
Exercise: tracing ownership through a sample structure

modules.title: Financial Crime Checks at the Gateway
modules.summary: How to integrate anti-money laundering, counter-terrorist financing and sanctions checks into authorisation so that criminals and their associates do not gain a foothold in the regulated sector.
objectives: Integrate financial crime risk assessment into the authorisation process
Assess source of funds and source of wealth for owners and capital
Evaluate an applicant's planned AML/CFT and sanctions framework
syllabus: FATF standards on preventing criminals from owning or controlling firms
Source of funds, source of wealth and capital injections
Screening, intelligence sharing and engagement with the national FIU
Assessing the applicant's financial crime controls before go-live

modules.title: Cross-Border Authorisation and Supervisory Cooperation
modules.summary: How passporting and cross-border recognition regimes work, the respective roles of home and host authorities, and the cooperation needed to verify applicants and protect host-market customers.
objectives: Explain passporting, branch and cross-border services models
Assess the respective responsibilities of home and host authorities
Identify practical cooperation steps and when host intervention applies
syllabus: Freedom of establishment versus freedom to provide services
Notification processes, branches, subsidiaries and third-country firms
Memoranda of understanding and verification with foreign authorities
Case study: a cross-border firm causing host-market concern

modules.title: Licence Variations, Conditions and Decisions
modules.summary: Brings the programme together: varying and restricting permissions, imposing conditions, refusing or withdrawing a licence, and handing a new firm over to supervision.
objectives: Assess applications to vary, extend or cancel permissions
Choose between conditions, phased authorisation and refusal
Formulate and document a defensible authorisation recommendation
syllabus: Variations of permission, restrictions and voluntary cancellation
Refusals, withdrawals, representations and appeals
Handover to supervision and early post-authorisation engagement
Workshop: assessing a marginal application end to end

related.title: Fit and Proper Assessments: Approving Owners, Directors and Key Function Holders
related.summary: An eight-module practitioner programme on assessing owners, controllers, directors and key function holders, from evidence gathering and interviews to defensible decisions.

related.title: Conducting Regulatory Investigations: From Referral to Outcome
related.summary: An eight-module practitioner programme taking enforcement staff through a regulatory investigation, from referral and powers to compelled interviews, findings and outcome.

related.title: Crisis Management and Resolution
related.summary: A ten-module programme preparing supervisors for firm and system-wide stress, from early intervention and recovery and resolution planning to crisis communication and a live simulation.

related.title: Enforcement and Sanctions
related.summary: A ten-module programme taking enforcement and supervisory staff through the full life of an enforcement case, from triage and evidence to sanctions, settlement and cooperation.

related.title: Policy-Making and Rule-Making
related.summary: An eight-module programme covering the full policy cycle, from problem definition and cost-benefit analysis to drafting, standards implementation and post-implementation review.

related.title: Assessing Board Effectiveness
related.summary: An eight-module programme showing supervisors how to assess how a board really works, from papers and decisions to culture and challenge, culminating in case-study interviews.
